# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete – Updated 87)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; **spring of third year (present narrative through auction and financial crisis)** (narrative extends into future years); present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Harrowgate, parsonage, forge, Brompton, barracks neighbourhood, City church, Gloster Coffee House, Portsmouth, Threadneedle Street, Fulham Road, St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), Provence, Elba, Notre Dame, Stock Exchange

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist
- **Secret Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rawdon in snug little Brompton lodgings; wearing new gloves, shawls, rings, watch purchased by Rawdon; marriage revealed through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs
- **Piano Situation**: Discontented with hired piano; attempted to purchase small square piano at Russell Square auction (former instrument from Amelia Sedley's sitting-room); bid unsuccessful as Captain Dobbin's agent (operating for Dobbin's benefit to Amelia) outbid her
- **Contact with Miss Crawley**: Controlled household access at Park Lane; read Morning Post to Miss Crawley; now denied access as door kept by Mr. Bowls; letters sent back unopened

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church by special license
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Living with Rebecca in Brompton lodgings furnished luxuriously; awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; anxiously considers possibility she may not recover (potential loss of fifty thousand pounds inheritance); denied door access by Mr. Bowls; servants cannot gain lodgment in Park Lane house; letters unopened
- **Financial Strain**: Household suffers from lack of ready money; reads Gazette; discovered Lieutenant G. Osborne promoted to Captain by purchase (vice Smith); this news prompted visit to Russell Square regarding Osborne
- **Debt Note**: Played billiards at Cocoa-Tree, won two hundred pounds from George Osborne

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Gave final scream and fainted upon learning Rebecca married to Rawdon; suffered one fit of hysterics succeeding another; doctor and apothecary summoned; confined to bed under care of Mrs. Bute Crawley as nurse
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: "Long in coming-to"; month has elapsed since revelation; never stirs out, unwell; door kept by Mr. Bowls; access denied to Rawdon and Rebecca; letters sent back unopened; remains under Mrs. Bute's continued presence

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; arrived at Park Lane by Portsmouth mail morning of marriage revelation crisis
- **Actions and Positioning**: Declared Rebecca "artful little hussy"; considered Rawdon profligate; positioned herself as nurse to Miss Crawley; took vacant room at Park Lane to attend her; remains present continuously; guards access to Miss Crawley; has not left her side; characterized by Crawley couple as source of "evil auguries"

**Miss Briggs** [CHARACTER]
- Found letter on Rebecca's pincushion containing marriage revelation early morning; read "affecting and interesting document"; reinstated as first confidante of Miss Crawley; reported intelligence of clandestine marriage to Mrs. Bute upon arrival; participated in Miss Crawley's crisis; shuddered and left room when Sir Pitt heard news and broke into fury

**Sir Pitt Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; now widower; made marriage proposal to Rebecca
- **Response to Marriage Revelation**: Upon learning Rebecca married to Rawdon, broke out into fury of language; became frenzied old man, wild with hatred and insane with baffled desire; subsequently ransacked Rebecca's room at Queen's Crawley, destroying her belongings (few days after Lady Crawley's burial)

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul; confirmed engagement to George; completely innocent of Rebecca and Rawdon's situation; trusts George completely
- **Financial Crisis**: Father John Sedley ruined; name proclaimed as defaulter on Stock Exchange; bankruptcy and commercial extermination followed; forced to hide head with wife and daughter at St. Adelaide Villas (Anna-Maria Road West), small cottage near Fulham Road
- **Father's Status**: All speculations failed; merchants broke; funds rose when he calculated they would fall; kept own sad counsel; final crash swept away fortune; family lived in apparent normalcy until collapse
- **Piano**: Owned small square piano (now sold at auction) formerly in sitting-room at Russell Square

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; now ruined man; proclaimed defaulter on Stock Exchange; declared bankrupt and commercially exterminated
- **Collapse Details**: All ventures failed; merchants broke; funds behaved unexpectedly; kept sad counsel about troubles; lived quietly in Russell Square with wife and daughter until final crash; now hiding at St. Adelaide Villas with family; aided in past by young stockbrokers (Messrs. Dale, Spiggot, and Dale of Threadneedle Street)

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports; adored by men; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Engagement**: Engaged to Amelia; furious upon learning regiment knows; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"
- **Status Change**: Promoted from Lieutenant to Captain by purchase (vice Smith, who exchanges); announcement read in Gazette by Rawdon
- **Debt with Rawdon**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards at Cocoa-Tree

**Captain William Dobbin** [CHARACTER]
- Carried off George Osborne from billiards; cannot play piano nor dance on tight rope
- **Action at Auction**: Served as agent bidding for small square piano at Russell Square auction; successfully outbid Rawdon's agent; acquired piano for Amelia Sedley's benefit (likely to provide her replacement instrument after financial crash)

**Other Characters**
- **Lady Crawley**: Deceased; Sir Pitt's wife; died during winter at Wilhaven; buried unwept and disregarded; Rebecca's room ransacked by Sir Pitt only few days after burial
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Witnessed proposal with Miss Briggs; oversees servants at Park Lane; wrote to Mrs. Bute Crawley reporting events
- **Miss Horrocks**: Butler's daughter at Queen's Crawley; took some of Rebecca's relics from boxes Sir Pitt flung open
- **Mr. Hammerdown**: Auctioneer at Russell Square auction; offered lots including "Portrait of gentleman on elephant" and small square piano
- **Mr. Blowman**: Auction assistant; presented lots for examination
- **Mr. Lewis**: Purchased small square piano at auction (agent of Captain Dobbin)
- **Mr. Bowls**: Doorkeeper at Park Lane; denies Rawdon and Rebecca access; returns their letters unopened
- **Mr. Clapp**: Clerk of Mr. Sedley; found domicile at St. Adelaide Villas with Sedley family
- **Mrs. Sedley**: Amelia's mother; living in reduced circumstances at St. Adelaide Villas
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant; butler purchased port wine for his cellar from Sedley's sale
- **Movie, Colan, Maric**: Secondary characters with minor narrative presence (weather and local observations; Maric rode from Bryngate to Gulton)
- **Colan Lindson**: Wife died of coughing sickness summer, buried at Bryngate

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)
- **MARRIAGE REVELATION OCCURRED**: Rebecca's secret marriage to Rawdon discovered through letter found on pincushion by Miss Briggs
- **MISS CRAWLEY'S CRISIS**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed; doctor and apothecary summoned; placed under Mrs. Bute Crawley's continuous nursing care; month elapsed; not "coming-to"; never stirs out
- **ACCESS DENIAL**: Mr. Bowls prevents Rawdon and Rebecca's entry to Park Lane; their letters returned unopened; Mrs. Bute remains continuously present
- **SIR PITT'S FURY AND DESTRUCTION**: Upon learning marriage, broke into fury; became wild and insane with baffled desire; ransacked Rebecca's room at Queen's Crawley, destroying belongings (days after Lady Crawley's burial)
- **REBECCA AND RAWDON'S POSITION**: Living in Brompton lodgings; awaiting Miss Crawley's recovery; suffering lack of ready money; both augur evil from Mrs. Bute's continued presence
- **RUSSELL SQUARE AUCTION**: Old house where Sedleys lived; site of liquidation of John Sedley's estate after financial ruin; items sold include rare wines (purchased by Mr. Osborne's butler), family plate (stockbrokers), and small square piano (acquired by Captain Dobbin for Amelia)
- **SEDLEY FAMILY COLLAPSE**: John Sedley proclaimed defaulter on Stock Exchange; bankruptcy followed; family forced to hide at St. Adelaide Villas near Fulham Road; Amelia remains unaware of broader events, absorbed in tender thoughts; wife Mrs. Sedley living in reduced circumstances
- **PIANO INCIDENT**: Rebecca attempted to purchase small square piano at auction (formerly Amelia's instrument); Captain Dobbin's agent successfully outbid her; piano delivered to Amelia's location; suggests Dobbin aware of and responding to Sedley family's distress
- **NARRATIVE CONTEXT**: Narrator observes opportunity for forgiveness was "denied to the young couple, doubtless in order that this story might be written"; references "wonderful adventures" that could not have occurred under Miss Crawley's comfortable forgiveness; notes overlap with Napoleonic events (eagles of Napoleon flying from Provence through Elba to Notre Dame)
